analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and file metadata against the indexed threat model and detailed T-041 evidence. No concrete regression is established in this scope. ProviderLoop+StartupPreload.swift:195-198 adds only hold-specific logging; the existing drain guard still returns cancelled. ProviderLoop+StartupShutdown.swift:26-32 changes drain precedence so shutdown can supersede an add-on hold, while retaining endpoint shutdown, preload cancellation and App Attest worker termination. Later teardown still drains requests/native owners and unloads models. ProviderLoop+Trust.swift:107-108 adds an add-on hold snapshot to local daemon diagnostics without changing connection-authorization clearing or trust-status handling. ProviderLoop.swift:484-497 introduces hold bookkeeping, task ownership, a local IPC server and authentication/time test seams; declarations alone do not establish the IPC security controls.
Integration must examine ProviderLoop+AddonHold, AddonIPCServer, AddonHoldBook and ProviderDrain definitions: peer authentication, socket/path protection, bounded leases, generation-safe cancellation, and whether release can undo lifecycle shutdown. Also trace the run() caller's handling of preload .cancelled under an add-on hold to distinguish intended deferred service from an unintended termination/restart loop, and inspect addonHoldSnapshot for credential or stable-identity disclosure. These questions concern TB-003/TB-007 availability, T-010/T-029 resource ownership, and TB-011/T-053 authorization continuity; they are not proven vulnerabilities. No supplied change directly alters prompt encryption, cache scope/crypto (T-008/T-041), model integrity, billing, or privileged fan authority. Missing hold/IPC implementations and callers limit the security conclusion.
